mainTopic: Eating before תפילה, prayers of the בית המדרש, sickbed teachings, and the origins of שמונה עשרה and ברכת המינים
overview: This amud opens with a story: רב אויא missed רב יוסף's lecture, and אביי's questions show that the reason was halachic, not disrespect. The rules involved are רב הונא's (no eating before מוסף) and רבי יוחנן's (no davening before the ציבור), which רבי אבא limits to someone davening with the ציבור. The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows neither רב הונא nor רבי יהושע בן לוי (no eating before מנחה). A משנה then tells of the short prayers רבי נחוניא בן הקנה said on entering and leaving the בית המדרש, and a ברייתא gives their full wording. Two sickbed stories follow. רבי אליעזר teaches his students paths to עולם הבא. רבי יוחנן בן זכאי cries before facing the Divine judgment and blesses his students with מורא שמים. A new משנה gives views on saying the full or abbreviated שמונה עשרה, רבי אליעזר's warning against prayer that is קבע, a short prayer for a place of danger, and how a traveler faces בית קדשי הקדשים. The גמרא explains what the eighteen blessings correspond to and how far to bow. It then explains that ברכת המינים was added later in יבנה by שמואל הקטן, who forgot it the next year; the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אויא misses the lecture and אביי tries to calm רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא was ill and missed רב יוסף's lecture. The next day אביי wants to calm רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא was weak and did not come to רב יוסף's lecture. The next day, when he came, אביי wanted to settle רב יוסף's mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. It is setting up a conversation that will explain why רב אויא was absent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Missing your רבי's lecture could look like disrespect. אביי plans to question רב אויא in front of רב יוסף so the real reason comes out. That conversation will bring up several laws about eating and davening.

keyTerms.meaning: The public lecture, usually given on שבת
To settle or calm his mind (to appease him)

phrases.english: Rav Avya was weak (ill)
and did not come to Rav Yosef's lecture.
The next day, when he came,

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא אַבָּיֵי לְאַנּוֹחֵי דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: Abaye wanted to calm Rav Yosef's mind.
phrases.notes: אביי will draw out the reason through questions.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַוְיָא חֲלַשׁ וְלָא אֲתָא לְפִרְקָא דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story connected to the earlier discussion of מוסף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the story; no ruling yet

steps.title: אביי asks why רב אויא did not come
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב אויא why he missed the lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why did the Master not come to the lecture?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a direct question so the reason for the absence will come out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack. Its goal is to give רב אויא a chance to explain himself in front of רב יוסף.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲתָא מָר לְפִרְקָא?
phrases.english: Why did the Master not come to the lecture?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲתָא מָר לְפִרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the plan from step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רב אויא missed the lecture

steps.title: רב אויא explains he felt too weak
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers that his heart was weak and he could not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because my heart was weak and I was not able to come.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא gives his reason: he felt faint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'My heart was weak' means he felt faint from hunger or weakness. This answer leads to the next question: why didn't he just eat?

keyTerms.meaning: My heart was weak (I felt faint)

phrases.english: He (Rav Avya) said to him:
Because my heart was weak and I was not able.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּהֲוָה חֲלִישׁ לִבַּאי וְלָא מָצֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He felt faint and could not come

steps.title: Why not eat something and then come?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges him: you could have eaten something and then come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why didn't you eat something and come?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the excuse, since eating would have fixed the weakness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem was hunger, the simple fix is to eat. So the excuse seems weak, unless something stopped him from eating.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
Why did you not eat something and come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי לָא טְעַמְתְּ מִידֵּי וַאֲתֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the excuse given in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weakness from hunger is solved by eating, so it should not have kept him away

steps.title: רב הונא forbids eating before מוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers that רב הונא forbids eating anything before davening מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold like רב הונא? רב הונא said: A person may not taste anything before he davens מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא defends himself with a law: he was not allowed to eat before מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lecture was before מוסף, so by רב הונא's rule he could not eat first. That explains why eating was not an option for him.

phrases.english: He (Rav Avya) said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא?
phrases.english: Does the Master not hold that ruling of Rav Huna?
For Rav Huna said:
A person is forbidden to taste anything
before he davens the Musaf prayer!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Cites a halachic rule that blocks the suggested solution
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating before מוסף is forbidden according to רב הונא
steps.whyThisMatters: רב הונא's rule comes back in step 9, where the גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow it.

steps.title: Daven מוסף alone first, then eat and come
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests he should have davened מוסף by himself, eaten, and then come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Master should have davened מוסף alone, eaten something, and come.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a way around רב הונא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem is eating before מוסף, then daven מוסף first as a יחיד. Then eating is allowed and he could still reach the lecture.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
The Master should have
prayed the Musaf prayer individually,
and eaten something, and come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמָר לְצַלּוֹיֵי צְלוֹתָא דְּמוּסָפִין בְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב הונא for now but offers a way around it
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב הונא's rule forced him to stay home
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Davening מוסף alone first would have made eating allowed

steps.title: רבי יוחנן forbids davening before the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers that רבי יוחנן forbids davening one's own תפילה before the ציבור davens.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold like רבי יוחנן, who said: A person may not daven his own תפילה before the ציבור's תפילה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא blocks אביי's suggestion with a second law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Davening מוסף alone before the ציבור would be davening ahead of the community. רבי יוחנן forbids that, so the shortcut fails.

keyTerms.meaning: That he put first (go ahead of)

phrases.english: He (Rav Avya) said to him:
And does the Master not hold
that which Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person is forbidden
to put his prayer before the community's prayer?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could daven מוסף alone early
steps.terutzMaskana: Davening before the ציבור is forbidden according to רבי יוחנן

steps.title: רבי אבא limits רבי יוחנן's rule to someone with the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי אבא said רבי יוחנן's rule applies only to someone davening with a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wasn't it said about this that רבי אבא said: They taught this only about someone in a ציבור?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב אויא's second reason by narrowing רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule only stops someone who is part of the ציבור from davening ahead of them. Someone davening on his own at home is not bound by it. So רב אויא could have davened early, eaten, and come. Still, his reason for missing the lecture is now clear, and that was אביי's goal.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught it about someone in a community

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא does not cancel רבי יוחנן's rule. He only narrows it to the case of someone davening with a ציבור.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
Was it not stated about it:
Rabbi Abba said:
They taught it regarding one in a congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּצִבּוּר שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense of step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבי יוחנן's rule for someone not davening with the ציבור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן's rule was stated only for someone who is part of a ציבור
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's questions brought out רב אויא's real reason for missing the lecture. Along the way we learned רב הונא's rule (no eating before מוסף), רבי יוחנן's rule (do not daven before the ציבור), and רבי אבא's limit (it applies only to someone with the ציבור).

steps.title: The הלכה follows neither רב הונא nor רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules against רב הונא (no eating before מוסף) and against רבי יהושע בן לוי (no eating once מנחה time arrives).
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is not like רב הונא and not like רבי יהושע בן לוי. Not like רב הונא, in the rule we just quoted. Not like רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: Once the time of מנחה arrives, a person may not taste anything before he davens מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final ruling. It rejects two rules that forbid eating before davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule about מוסף was already quoted in step 5, so the גמרא just points back to it. רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule about מנחה is new here, so the גמרא quotes it in full. Neither prohibition is accepted as הלכה.
steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: the הלכה follows neither רב הונא's ban on eating before מוסף nor רבי יהושע בן לוי's ban on eating once מנחה time arrives.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not like Rav Huna
and not like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
Like Rav Huna: that which we said.
Like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Once the time of the Mincha prayer has arrived,
a person is forbidden to taste anything
before he davens the Mincha prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּרַב הוּנָא וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on רב הונא's rule from step 5 and adds a parallel rule about מנחה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither prohibition on eating before מוסף or before מנחה is accepted as הלכה
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling on whether eating is allowed before מוסף and מנחה.

steps.title: משנה: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's short prayer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports that רבי נחוניא בן הקנה said a short prayer when he entered and when he left the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה used to say a short prayer when he entered the בית המדרש and when he left it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes something רבי נחוניא בן הקנה regularly did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are not the fixed daily תפילות. They are short personal prayers said at the door of the בית המדרש. The next lines explain why he said them.

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakana would pray
upon his entering the study hall and upon his leaving
a short prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He said a short prayer when entering and when leaving the בית המדרש

steps.title: Why say a prayer there?
steps.stepSummary: People ask רבי נחוניא what reason there is for such a prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What place is there for this prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: People question the purpose of his prayer. This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Prayers like this were usually said in dangerous places. A בית המדרש is not dangerous, so the prayer seemed unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What room / what reason is there?

phrases.english: They said to him:
What room is there for this prayer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מָקוֹם לִתְפִלָּה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the practice described in step 10

steps.title: A prayer to avoid mistakes, and thanks on leaving
steps.stepSummary: On entering he prays that no mistake should happen through him. On leaving he thanks ה׳ for his portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: When I enter, I pray that no mishap should happen through me. When I leave, I give thanks for my portion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחוניא explains both prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger in the בית המדרש is spiritual: ruling wrongly in הלכה. So on entering he asks to be protected from that. On leaving he thanks ה׳ that his lot is to sit and learn.

keyTerms.meaning: A mishap, a mistake (here, a wrong ruling)

phrases.english: He said to them:
Upon my entering, I pray

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע דְּבַר תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדִי.
phrases.english: that no mishap should happen through me.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִיצִיאָתִי אֲנִי נוֹתֵן הוֹדָאָה עַל חֶלְקִי.
phrases.english: And upon my leaving, I give thanks for my portion.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּכְנִיסָתִי אֲנִי מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע דְּבַר תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The entry prayer protects against mistakes in הלכה; the exit prayer thanks ה׳ for his lot

steps.title: ברייתא: The full text of the entry prayer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the exact words רבי נחוניא said when entering the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When entering, what does he say? 'May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that no mishap happen through me, that I not stumble in a matter of הלכה, and that my friends rejoice in me. That I not call impure pure or pure impure. That my friends not stumble in a matter of הלכה, and that I rejoice in them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that spells out the exact wording of the entry prayer from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer asks for more than avoiding his own mistakes. It also asks that his friends not err, and that they rejoice in each other. The example of טמא and טהור shows the kind of mistake he feared: a wrong ruling in הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
I will stumble, make a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: רבי נחוניא's entry prayer asks to avoid mistakes in הלכה, for himself and for his friends, so that they can rejoice in one another.

phrases.english: Gemara:
The Rabbis taught:
Upon his entering, what does he say?
"May it be Your will, ה׳ my God,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע דְּבַר תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדִי,
phrases.english: that no mishap should happen through me,
and that I not stumble in a matter of halacha,
and that my colleagues rejoice in me,
and that I not call the impure pure,
nor the pure impure.
And that my colleagues not stumble in a matter of halacha,
and that I rejoice in them."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ מַהוּ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exact wording of the entry prayer mentioned in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The full text of the entry prayer

steps.title: The prayer said when leaving the study hall
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes by giving the words רבי נחוניא בן הקנה said when leaving the בית המדרש: thanks to ה׳ that his life is spent in Torah and not in idleness.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he left, what did he say? "I thank You, ה׳ my God, that You put my portion among those who sit in the בית המדרש and not among those who sit on street corners. I get up early and they get up early. I get up early for Torah, and they get up early for empty things. I work hard and they work hard. I work hard and get a reward, and they work hard and get no reward. I run and they run. I run toward the life of עולם הבא, and they run toward the pit of destruction."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא already gave the entering prayer. Now it gives the exact words רבי נחוניא said on his way out of the בית המדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fills in the second half of the משנה's report: the exit prayer is a תודה, a thank-you. It is built on three matching pairs: rising early, working hard, and running. In each pair both groups do the same action, but only the Torah learner's effort leads somewhere lasting.

keyTerms.meaning: My portion, my lot in life
People who sit idly on street corners

steps.whatToRemember: Entering prayer = asking that no mistake happen through me. Exiting prayer = thanking ה׳ for my portion among Torah learners.

phrases.english: Upon his leaving, what does he say?
phrases.notes: Same question-and-answer format the ברייתא used for the entering prayer.

phrases.english: "I give thanks before You, ה׳ my God,
that You placed my portion among those who sit in the study hall,
and did not place my portion among those who sit on street corners.
For I rise early, and they rise early.
phrases.notes: First pair: the same action with a different purpose.

phrases.english: I rise early for words of Torah,
and they rise early for empty matters.
I toil and they toil.
I toil and receive a reward,
and they toil and do not receive a reward.
I run and they run.
phrases.notes: Third pair: where each life is heading.

phrases.english: I run to the life of the World to Come,
and they run to the pit of destruction."

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיצִיאָתוֹ מַהוּ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 13 by giving the exit wording to match the entry wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On leaving the בית המדרש, one thanks ה׳ for placing his portion among Torah learners rather than among idle people.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's students ask for paths of life
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that when רבי אליעזר was sick, his students visited him and asked him to teach them how to earn עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When רבי אליעזר became sick, his students came in to visit him. They said to him: "Our teacher, teach us the paths of life, so that through them we will earn the life of עולם הבא."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story connected to the theme of עולם הבא and prayer. Here it only sets up the students' request; רבי אליעזר's answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link to what came before is the shared goal: רבי נחוניא ended with "I run to the life of עולם הבא," and these students ask exactly how to get there. Their request asks for practical guidance, not just more learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Paths of life, guidelines for how to live
The life of the World to Come

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: When Rabbi Eliezer fell ill,
his students came in to visit him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבֵּינוּ לַמְּדֵנוּ אוֹרְחוֹת חַיִּים
phrases.english: They said to him: Our teacher, teach us paths of life,
and we will merit through them the life of the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A thematic link: after רבי נחוניא's "running to עולם הבא," the students ask how to earn עולם הבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Practical guidelines for living that will earn עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's four instructions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tells his students to guard the honor of others, keep their children from הגיון, seat them before תלמידי חכמים, and know before Whom they stand in prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "Be careful with the honor of your friends. Keep your children away from הגיון. Seat them among the knees of תלמידי חכמים. And when you pray, know before Whom you are standing. Because of this you will earn the life of עולם הבא."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his students' request with four instructions. He promises that keeping them leads to עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four instructions cover how you treat others, how you raise your children (two instructions), and how you pray. The last one, "know before Whom you stand," is likely why the story appears in this perek about תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor of your friends or fellow people
A word with several explanations; see the note below
Between the knees of Torah scholars, meaning sitting close to them as students
Know before Whom you are standing

steps.confusionAlert: "הגיון" does not simply mean "stop thinking logically." The מפרשים explain it in different ways. רש"י explains that children should not be trained too much in plain reading of מקרא alone. Sefaria's translation connects it to reasoning about verses in a way that leads toward heresy.
steps.whyThisMatters: "דעו לפני מי אתם עומדים" became a famous guiding line for proper focus in תפילה. It is often written above the ארון קודש in shuls.

phrases.english: He said to them: Be careful with the honor of your friends,
and keep your children away from הגיון,
phrases.notes: The meaning of הגיון is explained differently by the מפרשים (see the confusion alert).

phrases.english: and seat them between the knees of Torah scholars,
and when you pray,
know before Whom you are standing.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִשְׁבִיל כָּךְ תִּזְכּוּ לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: And because of this you will merit the life of the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: הִזָּהֲרוּ בִּכְבוֹד חַבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the students' request from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Four instructions: honor others, keep children from הגיון, place them before תלמידי חכמים, and pray with awareness of ה׳'s presence. Together these earn עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי cries and his students ask why
steps.stepSummary: A second story: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי cried when his students visited him on his sickbed. They praised him with three titles and asked why he was crying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when רבי יוחנן בן זכאי became sick, his students came in to visit him. When he saw them, he started to cry. His students said to him: "Lamp of Israel, right-hand pillar, mighty hammer, why are you crying?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second, similar sickbed story about רבי אליעזר's own teacher. This step only sets up the question; his answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students are surprised. Someone as great as their teacher, as the three titles show, should have nothing to fear. Their question prepares for רבי יוחנן בן זכאי's explanation of why even a great צדיק feels fear before standing in judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: Lamp of Israel, the one who gives light to the Jewish people
The right-hand pillar, the main support
The mighty hammer, a powerful Torah mind who breaks open difficult questions

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume a reason for his crying yet. The גמרא gives his answer in steps 18–20.

phrases.english: And when Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill,
his students came in to visit him.
As soon as he saw them, he began to cry.
His students said to him:
"Lamp of Israel, right-hand pillar, mighty hammer,"
phrases.notes: Three titles of praise that show how surprising his crying was to them.

phrases.english: for what reason are you crying?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי נִכְנְסוּ תַּלְמִידָיו לְבַקְּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel sickbed story about רבי אליעזר's teacher, opening with the same scene of students visiting.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why such a great צדיק would be crying at the end of his life.

steps.title: Even a human king would make me cry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי begins answering why he is crying: even judgment by a mortal king would frighten him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them: If I were being led before a human king, who is here today and in the grave tomorrow, his anger, imprisonment, and killing would not last forever. I could also try to persuade or bribe him. Even so, I would cry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי begins his answer with a comparison. He first describes the less frightening case: facing a human king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king has limited power and a limited life. There might also be ways to change his decision, yet the encounter would still be frightening.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִילּוּ לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם
phrases.english: He said to them: If before a human king
they were leading me, who is here today
and in the grave tomorrow; if he were angry with me
his anger would not be eternal anger,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אוֹסְרֵנִי — אֵין אִיסּוּרוֹ אִיסּוּר עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: and if he imprisoned me, his imprisonment would not be eternal imprisonment,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם מְמִיתֵנִי — אֵין מִיתָתוֹ מִיתַת עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: and if he killed me, his killing would not be an eternal death,
and I could appease him with words

phrases.aramaic: וּלְשַׁחֲדוֹ בְּמָמוֹן, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן
phrases.english: and bribe him with money; even so
I would cry,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִילּוּ לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students’ question by beginning a comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even facing a mortal king would make him cry.

steps.title: Facing the King whose judgment endures
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי completes the comparison: he is about to face הקדוש ברוך הוא, whose judgment cannot be treated like a human king’s.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now they are leading me before the supreme King, the Holy One, Blessed be He, who lives forever. His anger, imprisonment, and killing can have eternal consequences, and I cannot appease Him with words or bribe Him with money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי turns to the far more frightening side of his comparison: standing before הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each limit he named for a human king is now reversed. This explains why the approaching judgment makes him cry.

keyTerms.meaning: the supreme King over all kings
the Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: And now that they are leading me before

phrases.aramaic: מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַי וְקַיָּים לְעוֹלָם וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים,
phrases.english: who lives and endures forever and ever,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם כּוֹעֵס עָלַי — כַּעֲסוֹ כַּעַס עוֹלָם,
phrases.english: if He is angry with me, His anger is eternal anger,
and if He imprisons me, His imprisonment is eternal imprisonment,
and if He kills me, His killing is an eternal death,
and I cannot appease Him with words
or bribe Him with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִים אוֹתִי לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses each feature of the human-king comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Divine judgment is far more serious than human judgment.

steps.title: I do not know which path awaits me
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי adds that he does not know whether his path leads to גן עדן or גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more than that: Two paths are before me, one to גן עדן and one to גיהנם. I do not know which one they are leading me along. Should I not cry?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי adds a personal reason for his tears: he does not know the outcome of his judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison explained why the judgment is serious. His uncertainty about his own path explains why he is frightened now.

phrases.english: And more than that, there are before me

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי דְרָכִים, אַחַת שֶׁל גַּן עֵדֶן
phrases.english: two paths, one to the Garden of Eden
and one to Gehenna, and I do not know
on which one they are leading me; should I not cry?!

steps.whatToRemember: His tears come from both the seriousness of judgment and uncertainty about his own outcome.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְפָנַי שְׁנֵי דְרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds uncertainty about his destination to the explanation of his tears.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He does not know which of the two paths awaits him.

steps.title: The students ask for a blessing
steps.stepSummary: After hearing his answer, the students ask רבי יוחנן בן זכאי to bless them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Our teacher, bless us.
steps.whatsHappening: The students make a new request. This sets up רבי יוחנן בן זכאי’s next teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They are no longer asking why he cried. They now ask what he wishes for them.

phrases.english: They said to him: Our teacher, bless us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבֵּינוּ, בָּרְכֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for his tears to a request for a blessing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What blessing will he give his students?

steps.title: Fear Heaven as much as people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי blesses his students that their מורא שמים should be like their fear of human beings.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: May it be God’s will that your fear of Heaven be like your fear of human beings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי answers the students’ request with a blessing about מורא שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing names a level the students can recognize from daily life: how strongly people care about being seen by others. His students will question whether that is enough.

phrases.english: He said to them: May it be God’s will
that fear of Heaven be upon you
like fear of human beings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁתְּהֵא מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם עֲלֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the blessing the students requested.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He wishes them fear of Heaven as strong as their fear of other people.

steps.title: Is that really enough?
steps.stepSummary: The students challenge the apparent modesty of the blessing: only as much fear of Heaven as fear of people?
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: Only that much?
steps.whatsHappening: The students are surprised by the comparison in the blessing. They ask whether רבי יוחנן בן זכאי meant to set the goal so low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They expected מורא שמים to be greater than fear of people. Their short question challenges the level he chose, not the value of מורא שמים.

phrases.english: His students said to him: Only that much?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: עַד כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the level stated in the blessing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of מורא שמים to fear of human beings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fear of Heaven sounds as though it should be greater, not merely equal.

steps.title: People already fear being seen by others
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי explains that matching one’s fear of people with מורא שמים would itself be a significant achievement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If only! Know that when a person commits a transgression, he says, ‘May no person see me.’
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי answers the students’ challenge with an everyday example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person committing an עבירה worries about another person seeing it. רבי יוחנן בן זכאי wishes that awareness of Heaven would affect the person just as strongly.

phrases.english: He said to them: If only! Know
that when a person commits a transgression, he says:
‘May no person see me.’

steps.whatToRemember: The blessing asks that awareness of Heaven become as real to a person as being seen by other people.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: וּלְוַאי, תֵּדְעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the seemingly small blessing is actually demanding.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People fear human witnesses even when committing an עבירה; equal awareness of Heaven would be meaningful.

steps.title: Final instructions at his death
steps.stepSummary: At his death, רבי יוחנן בן זכאי tells the students to move vessels because of טומאה and prepare a chair for חזקיהו מלך יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time of his death, he told them: Move the vessels because of טומאה, and prepare a chair for חזקיהו מלך יהודה, who is coming.
steps.whatsHappening: The story records two final instructions from רבי יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first instruction concerns the טומאה associated with his approaching death. The second announces the arrival of חזקיהו מלך יהודה; the text gives no further explanation here.

keyTerms.meaning: at the time of his death

phrases.english: At the time of his death, he said to them:
Move the vessels because of the impurity,
and prepare a chair for Hezekiah, king of Judah,
who is coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ, אָמַר לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the sickbed story with instructions given at his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Move the vessels because of טומאה and prepare a chair for חזקיהו מלך יהודה.

steps.title: Three views on the daily prayer
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה gives three views: always say the full שמונה עשרה, say an abbreviated version, or choose according to fluency.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבן גמליאל says a person says שמונה עשרה every day. רבי יהושע says an abridged version of it. רבי עקיבא says: If the prayer is fluent in a person’s mouth, say the full prayer; otherwise, say an abridged version.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins a discussion of daily תפילה. It presents three positions for the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל calls for the full שמונה עשרה each day, while רבי יהושע allows an abbreviated form. רבי עקיבא makes the choice depend on whether the person can say the prayer fluently.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who requires the full daily prayer
the sage who states the abbreviated option
the sage who makes the choice depend on fluency
an abbreviated form of that prayer
his prayer is fluent in his mouth

phrases.english: Mishna: Rabban Gamliel says:
Each and every day a person recites
the eighteen-blessing prayer. Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: מֵעֵין שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: An abridged version of the eighteen-blessing prayer. Rabbi Akiva says:
If his prayer is fluent in his mouth,
he recites the eighteen-blessing prayer; and if not,
an abridged version of the eighteen-blessing prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the sickbed story and opens a new משנה about daily תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה presents three positions on saying the full or abbreviated שמונה עשרה.

steps.title: A fixed prayer can lose its sense of pleading
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says that when someone makes prayer קבע, it is not תחנונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: One who makes his prayer fixed—his prayer is not supplication.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds רבי אליעזר’s warning about the way a person prays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He contrasts prayer treated as קבע with prayer offered as תחנונים. This line does not yet explain exactly what behavior counts as קבע.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הָעוֹשֶׂה תְּפִלָּתוֹ קֶבַע —
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: One who makes his prayer fixed—
his prayer is not supplication.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הָעוֹשֶׂה תְּפִלָּתוֹ קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about prayer after the three views on שמונה עשרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer made קבע is not תחנונים.

steps.title: A brief prayer in a dangerous place
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע gives a short prayer for someone walking in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says that one walking in a dangerous place prays a brief prayer, asking God to save His people, keep their needs before Him at every transition, and hear their prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a prayer to say when danger makes a full prayer difficult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a specific brief prayer for the dangerous situation. The משנה supplies its wording here.

keyTerms.meaning: a transition; a phrase whose precise meaning needs clarification

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: הַהוֹלֵךְ בִּמְקוֹם סַכָּנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: One walking in a dangerous place
prays a brief prayer and says:
“Save, Lord, Your people,
the remnant of Israel;
at every transition,
may their needs be before You.
Blessed are You, Lord, Who hears prayer.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: הַהוֹלֵךְ בִּמְקוֹם סַכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how prayer should feel to what someone says in danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone walking in a dangerous place says the specified תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.

steps.title: How a rider directs prayer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a sequence for a rider: dismount, turn the face if dismounting is impossible, or direct the heart if turning is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: One riding a donkey should dismount and pray. If he cannot dismount, he should turn his face. If he cannot turn his face, he should direct his heart toward בית קדשי הקדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now addresses someone praying while riding and gives a fallback for each physical difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rider first tries to dismount. If that is impossible, he turns his face; if even that is impossible, he directs his heart toward בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקׇּדָשִׁים.

phrases.english: If he was riding a donkey—

phrases.aramaic: יֵרֵד וְיִתְפַּלֵּל, וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לֵירֵד —
phrases.english: he should dismount and pray; if he cannot dismount—
he should turn his face.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו —
phrases.english: And if he cannot turn his face—
he should direct his heart toward
the Holy of Holies.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל הַחֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a brief prayer in danger to the physical direction of prayer during travel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rider follows the available option for directing prayer, ending with directing the heart toward בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקׇּדָשִׁים when necessary.

steps.title: Directing the heart while traveling by water
steps.stepSummary: A person on a ship or raft directs the heart toward בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקׇּדָשִׁים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One traveling on a ship or a raft should direct his heart toward בית קדשי הקדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a water-travel case and tells the traveler where to direct his heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The preceding case ended with directing the heart when physical turning was impossible. Here the משנה gives that instruction directly for a traveler on a ship or raft.

phrases.english: If he was traveling on a ship or a raft—
he should direct his heart toward
the Holy of Holies.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בִּסְפִינָה אוֹ בְּאַסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the direction-of-prayer teaching from a rider to water travel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler on a ship or raft directs the heart toward בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקׇּדָשִׁים.

steps.title: Why are there eighteen blessings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמונה עשרה and asks what its eighteen blessings correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What do these eighteen correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion by returning to the earlier mention of שמונה עשרה. It sets up an explanation for the number eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a question, not yet an answer. It asks for a basis for the number of blessings, rather than asking how to pray while traveling.

phrases.english: Gemara: What do these eighteen correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה כְּנֶגֶד מִי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה’s travel rules, the גמרא returns to the earlier teaching about שמונה עשרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for the number eighteen in שמונה עשרה.

steps.title: Eighteen mentions in a psalm
steps.stepSummary: רבי הילל explains the number eighteen through mentions of God in a psalm of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הילל, son of רבי שמואל בר נחמני, says the eighteen blessings correspond to eighteen mentions of God in “הבו לה׳ בני אלים.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to what the eighteen blessings correspond to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer connects the number of blessings to a count in a psalm. It explains the number, not the wording of each blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: opening words of the psalm being counted

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani, said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה אַזְכָּרוֹת שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד
phrases.english: Corresponding to eighteen mentions of God’s name that David said
in “Give to the Lord, sons of the mighty.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighteen blessings correspond to eighteen mentions of God in the psalm.

steps.title: Eighteen mentions in קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different count that corresponds to the eighteen blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says they correspond to eighteen mentions of God in קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents another answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף keeps the method of counting mentions of God. He changes the text being counted from a psalm to קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה אַזְכָּרוֹת שֶׁבִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: Corresponding to eighteen mentions of God’s name in the recitation of Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the count of eighteen.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighteen blessings correspond to eighteen mentions of God in קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Eighteen joints in the spine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי connects the eighteen blessings to the spine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום reports רבי יהושע בן לוי’s answer: they correspond to eighteen joints in the spine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a third answer to what the eighteen blessings correspond to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer changes the kind of comparison. Instead of counting words in another text, it counts parts of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage whose teaching is reported

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum said in the name of
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
Corresponding to eighteen joints in the spine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third way to account for the number eighteen.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighteen blessings correspond to eighteen joints in the spine.

steps.title: How far to bow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a measure for bowing during prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום also reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: One who prays must bow until all the joints of the spine protrude.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the mention of the spine to a related teaching about bowing in prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spine is now part of a practical instruction, not a way to count blessings. The teaching describes how deep the bow should be.

keyTerms.meaning: that they protrude or become distinct

phrases.english: And Rabbi Tanḥum said in the name of
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
One who prays must bow
until all the joints in the spine protrude.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the shared subject of the spine to introduce a related rule about bowing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prays must bow until the joints of the spine protrude.

steps.title: A visible measure for bowing
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives another way to describe the depth of a bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: Bow until one can see an איסר opposite one’s heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another measure for how far to bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous measure described what happens to the spine. עולא describes what the person can see while bent forward.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Until he can see a small coin
opposite his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a different measure for the bow discussed in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bow far enough to see an איסר opposite one’s heart.

steps.title: Moving the head can suffice
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא states a less demanding measure for bowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: Once one has moved one’s head, one need not do more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a more lenient measure for the bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This measure asks for head movement rather than the depth described in the two previous teachings. The next statement will limit when this is enough.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Once he has moved his head—
he need not do more.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a less demanding measure for bowing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving the head can be sufficient.

steps.title: A condition on the head movement
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits when moving the head is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: That is when the person is exerting himself and appears like someone who has bowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא qualifies רבי חנינא’s more lenient measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Head movement alone is not automatically sufficient. The person must be making an effort, and the movement must look like a bow.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And that is when he is exerting himself,
and appears like someone who has bowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the circumstances in which רבי חנינא’s measure suffices.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The smaller movement suffices when the person exerts himself and appears to be bowing.

steps.title: The count appears to be nineteen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the assumption that the prayer contains eighteen blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these eighteen? They are nineteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier count and raises a problem: there appear to be nineteen blessings, not eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three earlier answers relied on a count of eighteen. This challenge asks how that count fits the number of blessings actually found in the prayer. The next step answers it.

phrases.english: Are these eighteen?!
They are nineteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bowing discussion and challenges the earlier assumption about the number of blessings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The premise that the prayer being discussed has eighteen blessings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it has nineteen blessings, the proposed correspondences to eighteen need an explanation.

steps.title: ברכת המינים was added later in יבנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that ברכת המינים was instituted later in יבנה. That is why the prayer has nineteen blessings even though it is called eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: The blessing against the heretics was instituted in יבנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 39 about why there are nineteen blessings. The answer is that one blessing was added later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original prayer had eighteen blessings, which is where the name שמונה עשרה comes from. ברכת המינים was added afterward in יבנה, so it does not erase the original count. The name stayed the same even after the number grew.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing against heretics and sectarians (today 'ולמלשינים')
The town where the Sanhedrin met after the Second Temple was destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the prayer was 'wrong' to be called eighteen. It really was eighteen blessings at first. The nineteenth was added later, and the original name stayed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
The blessing of the heretics was instituted in Yavne.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: בִּרְכַּת הַמִּינִים בְּיַבְנֶה תִּקְּנוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 39 about the count of eighteen versus nineteen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical explanation: the extra blessing was a later addition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count of eighteen seemed to contradict the nineteen blessings we actually say.
steps.terutzMaskana: The original eighteen stayed. ברכת המינים was added later in יבנה.

steps.title: What does the added blessing correspond to?
steps.stepSummary: The number eighteen was tied to hints in earlier sources. So the גמרא asks what the nineteenth blessing corresponds to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Corresponding to what did they institute it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. It sets up the next step, where three answers will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the eighteen blessings were linked to eighteen things: eighteen mentions of God's name in a תהלים chapter, eighteen in קריאת שמע, and eighteen vertebrae. Now that we have nineteen, we need a nineteenth hint in each of those sources.

phrases.english: Corresponding to what did they institute it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּנֶגֶד מִי תִּקְּנוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on Step 40's statement that a nineteenth blessing was added.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source hint for the nineteenth blessing that matches the earlier explanations of eighteen.

steps.title: A nineteenth hint for each source of eighteen
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי matches the nineteenth blessing to each earlier source: אל הכבוד הרעים in תהלים, the word אחד in קריאת שמע, and the small vertebra at the bottom of the spine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: According to רבי הלל son of רבי שמואל בר נחמני, it corresponds to 'The God of glory thunders.' According to רב יוסף, it corresponds to 'One' in קריאת שמע. According to what רבי תנחום said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, it corresponds to the small vertebra in the spine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three answers. Each one fits a different earlier explanation of the number eighteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the eighteen names of God in תהלים כ"ט, the extra one is 'אל' in 'אל הכבוד הרעים', which is a different name of God. For the eighteen names in קריאת שמע, the extra one is the word 'אחד'. For the eighteen vertebrae, the extra one is a small vertebra at the bottom of the spine.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One', the key word of the first פסוק of שמע
A vertebra (one bone of the spine)

steps.whatToRemember: Each earlier source for eighteen also has a hidden nineteenth: אל הכבוד in תהלים, אחד in שמע, and the small vertebra in the spine.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani,
it corresponds to 'The God of glory thunders.'
phrases.notes: In תהלים כ"ט, where the eighteen mentions of God's name appear

phrases.english: According to Rav Yosef,
it corresponds to 'One' in the Shema.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: According to what Rabbi Tanḥum said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
it corresponds to the small vertebra in the spine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי לְרַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each earlier source of eighteen has a nineteenth element: אל הכבוד הרעים, אחד, and the small vertebra.

steps.title: How the blessing against heretics was composed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that שמעון הפקולי arranged the eighteen blessings before רבן גמליאל in יבנה. When רבן גמליאל asked who could compose ברכת המינים, שמואל הקטן stood up and composed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: שמעון הפקולי arranged the eighteen blessings in order before רבן גמליאל in יבנה. רבן גמליאל said to the חכמים: Is there anyone who knows how to compose the blessing against the heretics? שמואל הקטן stood up and composed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the story behind רבי לוי's statement that ברכת המינים was made in יבנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eighteen blessings already existed. שמעון הפקולי set them in their proper order. A new blessing was then needed against the heretics. רבן גמליאל asked for someone qualified to write it, and שמואל הקטן, known for his great piety, did so.

keyTerms.meaning: שמעון the cotton merchant, who arranged the order of the blessings
A very humble and pious תנא who composed ברכת המינים

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains who wrote ברכת המינים and why it was given to someone known for piety. The next part of the story builds on this.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְעוֹן הַפָּקוֹלִי הִסְדִּיר שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרָכוֹת
phrases.english: Shimon HaPakuli arranged the eighteen blessings

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עַל הַסֵּדֶר בְּיַבְנֶה.
phrases.english: before Rabban Gamliel, in order, in Yavne.
Rabban Gamliel said to the Sages:
Is there any person who knows
how to compose the blessing of the heretics?
Shmuel HaKatan stood up and composed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁמְעוֹן הַפָּקוֹלִי הִסְדִּיר שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story behind Step 40's statement about יבנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eighteen blessings were arranged by שמעון הפקולי, and ברכת המינים was composed by שמואל הקטן in יבנה.

steps.title: The next year, he forgot the blessing
steps.stepSummary: The story continues: the following year, שמואל הקטן forgot the blessing he had composed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year, he forgot it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story and sets up the next move. The rest, about what happened after he forgot, continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line adds a new problem to the story. Even the person who wrote the blessing forgot it when leading the prayer. That leads into a question about what to do when a שליח ציבור skips this blessing.

phrases.english: The next year, he forgot it,

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשָׁנָה אַחֶרֶת שְׁכָחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא story from Step 43 and sets up the next development.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל הקטן forgot the blessing he had composed. The story continues on the next amud.
